cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: OK Rosie, shall we try to get some ideas together for our presentation on diet and

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: obesity?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: I can talk about the experiment I did to see if people can tell the difference between

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: real sugar and artificial sweeteners.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Where you have people drinks with either sugar or artificial sweeteners and they had to

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: say which they thought it was?

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Yeah.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: It took me ages to decide exactly how I'd organise it, especially how I could make sure

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: that people didn't know which drink I was giving them.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: It was hard to keep track of it all, especially as I had so many people doing it – I had

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: to make sure I kept a proper record of what each person had had.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: Yeah – I hadn't thought they would be able to, but most people could.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Then there's that experiment I did measuring the fat content of nuts, to see if the

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: nutritional information given on the packet was accurate.

cues.speaker: AM
cues.text: The one where you ground up the nuts and mixed them with a chemical to absorb the fat?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Yes.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: My results were a bit problematic – the fat content for that type of nut seemed much

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: lower than it said on the package. But I reckon the package information was right.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I think I should probably have ground up the nuts more than I did.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: It's possible that the scales for weighing the fat weren't accurate enough, too.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I'd really like to try the experiment again some time.
